original.description: Destroyed defences at Liège, 1914, as reproduced in the German illustrated history "Der Krieg 1914-19 in Wort und Bild".
original.photographer: Presse-Centrale, Berlin (agency credited on the plate)
original.date: 1914 (subject); the record gives the plate as "by 1919"
original.archive: Wikimedia Commons; the record cites "Der Krieg 1914-19 in Wort und Bild", Deutsches Verlagshaus Bong & Co., Berlin, 1919

colorization.status: not colorized. Recommendation: leave as it is — a halftone plate from a 1919 book; colour would be invention on top of a screen.

content_policy: ok, and now checked against the frame. A displaced armoured cupola in its crater, rubble, one figure standing at a distance. NO HUMAN REMAINS ARE VISIBLE. FRAME CONFIRMED 2026-08-29 (sand-y0u.7.1): the image was opened and looked at, not read about.
caption: Destroyed defences at Liège, 1914, as a German illustrated history showed them to German readers after the war.
credit: Original photograph: Presse-Centrale, Berlin; published in "Der Krieg 1914-19 in Wort und Bild", Deutsches Verlagshaus Bong & Co., Berlin, 1919; via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. CAUTION for the image review (sand-y0u.7): a plate in a victors’-eye illustrated history is a publication with a point of view, and neither the exact fort nor the exact date is on the record. The caption is written to say what the source is rather than to assert a place. The plate carries its own printed German caption, “Wirkung der 42-Zentimeter-Geschütze auf die Forts von Lüttich”, and a Presse-Centrale, Berlin credit — which is the framing the caption already gives it.
